findings.summary: The Maven lifecycle phases are listed as seven bare lines with no label or arrows, so the sequence is not readable as a lifecycle diagram.
findings.evidence:
validate
compile
test
package
verify
install
deploy
findings.fix: Add a caption such as 'Maven lifecycle (in order)' and render it as a flow: validate → compile → test → package → verify → install → deploy.

findings.summary: The Gradle row of the wrapper commands sits apart from its Windows equivalents, so the Unix and Windows commands are not paired by tool.
findings.evidence:
./mvnw clean package
./gradlew build
mvnw.cmd clean package
gradlew.bat build
Unix first, then Windows
findings.fix: Use a small table with rows Maven and Gradle and columns Unix and Windows. Also use the same Gradle package command as pages 5 and 6 (bootJar), or explain why build differs.

findings.summary: The Gradle package command is inconsistent across pages: page 2 uses `./gradlew build`, while pages 5 and 6 use `./gradlew bootJar`.
findings.fix: Use one command for the Gradle package step throughout, or note that build runs tests and assembles while bootJar only builds the jar.

findings.summary: The BOM is explained mostly in prose bullets with XML snippets, and one bullet holds several separate ideas (parent POM settings).
findings.evidence: Also sets plugin config, Java version, UTF-8, resource filtering
findings.fix: Move the parent POM provisions into a short table: BOM of tested versions, plugin config, Java version, UTF-8, resource filtering.

findings.summary: Two ways to get managed versions (parent versus imported BOM) are written as separate text sections rather than a compact comparison.
findings.evidence:
2. No parent allowed? Import the BOM
Company parent POM: import spring-boot-dependencies in <dependencyManagement>
findings.fix: Add a two-row table: starter-parent (default, also sets plugin config and Java version) versus imported BOM (versions only, used when a company parent POM already exists).

findings.summary: The mistakes paragraph is a prose dump with two separate ideas in it.
findings.evidence: Pinning explicit versions of managed libs causes a mismatch with the Boot BOM. Do not add a starter for every library: only what you need.
findings.fix: Split it into two one-line bullets: 'Pinning managed versions can drift from the BOM' and 'Add only the starters you need'.

findings.summary: The startup sequence is given as three separate lines without an ordered flow, and the main class code appears before the scan rule that explains why its package matters.
findings.evidence:
SpringApplication.run creates the ApplicationContext
Then runs auto-configuration
Then starts the embedded server
findings.fix: Show it as a flow: create ApplicationContext → auto-configuration → start embedded server.

findings.summary: The fat jar versus war table has a mislabeled row: 'Libs' mixes the plugin that builds the jar into the lib-handling cell, and 'Extra step' lists a command in one column and a class to extend in the other.
findings.evidence:
Libs | Nested, via spring-boot-maven-plugin / Boot Gradle plugin | Deployed into the container
Extra step | java -jar and go | Extend SpringBootServletInitializer
findings.fix: Split into Libs (nested in the jar / provided by the container), Built by (Boot plugin / standard war plugin), and Run (java -jar / deploy to the container plus extend SpringBootServletInitializer).

findings.summary: The cheat sheet annotation list pairs each annotation with its meaning on separate lines with no table, which is hard to scan.
findings.fix: Use a two-column table: annotation | role.

findings.summary: The 'Check yourself' answers are written as plain consecutive lines with no visible separation between question and answer, so a skimming learner cannot tell which is which.
findings.evidence:
The main class is in com.example.demo. A @RestController sits in com.example.api. The app starts fine, but its endpoint returns 404. Why?
Component scan covers only the main class's package and its sub-packages
findings.fix: Mark each answer explicitly (for example 'Answer:') or use Q/A pairs, so each question is clearly separated from its answer.
